items.title: Nvidia announces native GPU programming in Rust
items.summary: Nvidia has introduced a new framework for writing GPU kernels in Rust, allowing developers to leverage Rust's safety and concurrency features in high-performance computing. This development is significant as it opens up new possibilities for safer and more efficient GPU programming.

items.title: Training a 4B model to produce 81% faster query plans than Postgres
items.summary: A new AI model has been trained to generate query plans that are 81% faster than those produced by Postgres, showcasing the potential of AI in optimizing database performance. This advancement could significantly enhance the efficiency of data retrieval in applications reliant on relational databases.

items.title: One Year of Sponsored Servo Development
items.summary: The Servo project has marked a year of sponsored development, highlighting its progress and future goals in building a high-performance web engine. This initiative is crucial for developers interested in modern web technologies and the evolution of browser engines.

items.title: Keys Not Included: recovering the signing keys for US driver's license barcodes
items.summary: A recent investigation revealed vulnerabilities in the signing keys used for US driver's license barcodes, raising significant security concerns. Developers and engineers should be aware of these findings to enhance security measures in similar systems.

items.title: Developing provably correct Rust code with Verus
items.summary: The Verus project aims to enable the development of provably correct Rust code, addressing critical issues in software reliability. This is particularly important for developers working in safety-critical systems where correctness is paramount.
